newsitem.title: RUSSIA: FORECAST-Russia 1996 car output up 4.0 pct - analyst.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Russia 1996 car output up 4.0 pct - analyst.

text.p: Russian car production will rise four percent to 866,563 units in 1996 from 835,095 units in 1995, MC Securities Ltd (MCS) of London said on Wednesday.
Dagmar Bottenbruch, MCS research director, presented the forecast at an automotive conference in Moscow.
MCS also predicted output to rise 10 percent to 953,219 units in 1997, five percent to 1,000,880 units in 1998, four percent to 1,040,915 units in 1999 and two percent to 1,061,734 units in 2000.
"After an initial setback, the Russian autmotive industry actually started to recover much faster than the overall economy, and it has developed quite robustly," Bottenbruch said.
Car production fell 28 percent to roughly 798,800 units in 1994 from 1,102,700 units in 1990, according to MCS. No economic data were provided.
Russia's two largest carmakers will drive all of the growth in 1996, while the country's other five major manufacturers will report declines, MCS forecast.

Lada-manufacturer AO AvtoVAZ will raise output nine percent to 667,088 units in 1996 from 609,213 units in 1995, and AO Gorkovsky Avtomobilny Zavod will raise production one percent to 120,097 units in 1996 from 118,673 units in 1995, MCS forecast.
